description: A Go CLI tool (v1.1.7) for searching, browsing, and resuming Claude Code and Codex CLI sessions. Indexes JSONL transcript files into SQLite with FTS5, provides a Bubbletea TUI, and exposes an MCP server so Claude itself can query past sessions.
value_proposition: Provides full-text search and session browsing for ~/.claude/projects/ and ~/.codex/sessions/ transcripts in a single binary with no external runtime dependencies. Core differentiator: the MCP server enables Claude Code to search its own session history ('tell it to see what you have done'), and the 'resume' feature launches claude --resume in the correct directory with one keystroke. Explicitly positions against 'broken' existing tools that have incomplete schema support, no real search, and can't resume sessions.
target_audience: Individual developers who use Claude Code or Codex CLI heavily and want a terminal-native way to search past sessions, resume conversations, and give their AI agent memory of prior context. No GUI, no cloud, no SaaS - pure local CLI/TUI tool.

tech_stack.database: SQLite with FTS5 via modernc.org/sqlite (pure-Go, CGO-free)
other_deps: olebedev/when for natural language date parsing
tech_stack.distribution: Homebrew tap (neilberkman/tap), GitHub releases via goreleaser, single binary

repo_structure.cmd/ccrider/: CLI entry point (main.go), mcp/ subdirectory for MCP server
repo_structure.internal/core/: Business logic: db/ (schema, migrations, sessions, stats, FTS), importer/ (sync, progress), search/, session/, llm/ (summarizer, Anthropic/Bedrock providers, extractor), export/, config/, models/, terminal/
repo_structure.internal/interface/: Thin UI wrappers: cli/ (command handlers), tui/ (Bubbletea terminal UI)
repo_structure.pkg/ccsessions/: Public Claude Code JSONL parser library (reusable independently)
repo_structure.pkg/codexsessions/: Public Codex CLI session parser library
repo_structure.docs/: CONFIGURATION.md, MCP_SERVER.md, RESUME_PROMPT.md, plans/ (design doc, phase1 spec)
repo_structure.research/: schema.md (Claude Code JSONL format documentation), requirements.md (original requirements spec)

feature_overview.transcript_monitoring: Manual sync (ccrider sync) only - no daemon/watch mode yet (planned Phase 3). Incremental: mtime+size -> BLAKE3 hash -> parse chain for 3.9x speedup. Can handle 105MB JSONL lines.
feature_overview.search: SQLite FTS5 full-text search. Dual FTS tables: porter stemming for natural language, unicode61 for code symbols. Supports date filters (ISO 8601, relative, natural language: 'yesterday', '3-days-ago'), project filters, provider filters (claude/codex). Filter-only mode (no text query required).
feature_overview.tui: Bubbletea TUI with browse, search, and session view modes. Vim-style navigation (j/k, gg/G). Light and dark theme support. Press 'o' to open in new terminal (auto-detects Ghostty, iTerm, Terminal.app). Export session as Markdown ('e' key). Project-awareness: highlights sessions matching current directory.
feature_overview.session_resume: Press 'r' to resume - executes claude --resume <sessionId> in correct cwd. Also: 'ccrider resume <id>' CLI. Recovery mode: if original file deleted, starts new session with context from indexed history.
feature_overview.mcp_server: Built-in MCP server (ccrider serve-mcp). Tools: search_sessions, list_recent_sessions, get_session_messages, generate_session_anchor. generate_session_anchor creates diceware phrases for cross-session context tagging. Auto-syncs DB silently before each query. Read-only access.
feature_overview.llm_summarization: Optional. Hierarchical chunk-based summarizer (100 msg chunks, 10 overlap). Backends: Anthropic API (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY env var) or AWS Bedrock. Uses claude-haiku-4-5. Skips sessions < 5 messages.
feature_overview.multi_provider: Claude Code (~/.claude/projects/) and Codex CLI (~/.codex/sessions/) in single DB. [codex] tags in TUI. Provider filter param on all MCP tools and CLI.
feature_overview.export: Export session as Markdown. Repo-aware (default export to <repo>/.ccrider/exports/). CLI: ccrider export <id> (stdout by default).
feature_overview.session_recovery: When Claude Code auto-deletes session files (30-day default cleanup), ccrider still has the indexed content and can create a new recovery session with prior context.

community_signals.external_contributions: 3 PRs merged from external contributors: APE-147 (Codex response_item parsing fix), neilberkman (Codex support), Vladimir Istyufeev (BLAKE3 sync inspiration/PR #5), Marco Seguri (light theme)

health_metrics.version_cadence: Active: ~1-2 releases/month. Jumped from v0.2.6 to v0.9.0, then v0.10.0, v1.0.0, v1.1.x. Indicates fast iteration.

positioning.explicit_claim: Fixes broken existing tools: 100% schema coverage, multi-provider, SQLite FTS5, single binary, native resume, incremental sync
positioning.terminal_only: Deliberately terminal-native. No web UI, no Electron, no npm/pip dependencies.
positioning.local_first: All data stays local. No cloud sync, no account required.
positioning.mcp_angle: The 'killer feature' framing is the MCP server giving Claude Code memory of past sessions - 'when your coding agent forgets, tell it to see what you have done'
positioning.non_goals_implied: No GUI, no real-time watch daemon (manual sync only), no cloud features, not a macOS app
positioning.design_inspiration: Saša Jurić's Core/Interface pattern from Elixir community applied to Go

key_findings: ccrider is a pure terminal CLI/TUI competitor - no GUI, no macOS app. Its entire UX is within the terminal. This is a fundamentally different form factor from Contextify.
The MCP server is ccrider's strongest differentiator: Claude Code can search its own session history mid-conversation. Contextify has no MCP server integration.
ccrider supports session RESUME (launching claude --resume), which Contextify does not offer - this is a workflow feature Contextify's HUD model doesn't have.
ccrider has multi-provider support (Claude Code + Codex CLI) already shipped. Contextify has both but positions additional providers as roadmap.

LLM summarization in ccrider is optional and requires user to bring their own API key (Anthropic or AWS Bedrock). Contextify's summaries use Apple Intelligence on-device - a significant UX and privacy advantage.
ccrider has no real-time monitoring - it only syncs on demand (ccrider sync). Contextify's core value prop is real-time HUD monitoring. These are different use cases.
ccrider is distributed as a single Go binary via Homebrew. Contextify is a macOS app (DMG + App Store). Very different distribution and installation UX.
ccrider has 29 releases in 5 months showing high velocity, with external contributors and a Show HN post. Suggests growing community interest in this problem space.
ccrider's session recovery feature (indexed content survives Claude Code's 30-day file deletion) directly competes with Contextify's database-first persistence model.
ccrider explicitly calls out that it parses all 5 Claude Code message types including file-history-snapshot - suggesting schema completeness is a known pain point among users.
